name: Oben Rageclaw
summary: In Ban'ethil Barrow Den, Oben Rageclaw's spirit wanders, unable to wake or pass on. His sleeping body remains under the Gnarlpine furbolgs' control.

sections.title: A Slumber Desecrated
sections.body: Oben Rageclaw entered Ban'ethil Barrow Den to commune with nature and wander the Emerald Dream, as many Druids of the Claw do. When the Gnarlpine furbolgs fell to corruption and overran the barrows, Oben lay defenseless in his trance. A corrupted Gnarlpine shaman used dark rituals to take control of his comatose body. His spirit was left behind as an anguished ghost, unable to wake or pass on.

sections.title: Severing the Vessel
sections.body: Oben Rageclaw cannot reclaim his body from the shaman's control. Travelers moving through the dangerous tunnels can end his torment by finding and destroying the body the shaman commands. When that vessel falls, Oben's tortured ghost is released from the underground gloom and finds rest in the Emerald Dream.

faq.answer: Oben Rageclaw is a night elf Druid of the Claw whose ghost wanders Ban'ethil Barrow Den in Teldrassil, separated from his body by corrupted furbolgs.

faq.q: Why is Oben Rageclaw a ghost?
faq.answer: Oben Rageclaw became a ghost while he slept in a druidic trance, communing with the Emerald Dream. Gnarlpine furbolg shamans entered the den, used foul magic to control his body, and trapped his spirit outside it.
Oben's body lies deeper in Ban'ethil Barrow Den's winding corridors, under the control of the Gnarlpine shamans who corrupted the den.

faq.q: What happens after Oben's body is destroyed?
faq.answer: When Oben's body is destroyed, the Gnarlpine shamans' hold over him is broken. His spirit can leave Teldrassil and find rest in the Emerald Dream.

angles.text: As a druid, Oben's fate shows how vulnerable druids are while communing with the Emerald Dream in a trance, when sacred barrow dens are undefended.
As a night elf, you see how deeply the Gnarlpine furbolgs' corruption has touched Teldrassil's native denizens and sacred sanctuaries.
